name: Third World
scope: The Third World as a political idea, as the defining sources present it: the emancipatory, anticolonial and internationalist project of the formerly colonised and non-aligned states of Asia, Africa and Latin America from the Bandung Conference (1955) through the Tricontinental (1966) and the 1974 call for a New International Economic Order, with its demands for self-determination, non-interference, non-alignment in the Cold War, South-South cooperation and a fairer world economy. It does not cover the term as a mere economic label for poor countries or as a geographic list (Yapp's second and third senses), Mao's Three Worlds Theory, nor the narrower doctrines with their own entries (third-worldism, Third World socialism, Maoist third-worldism).

summary: The Third World, as an idea, was the political project of the formerly colonised and non-aligned states of Asia, Africa and Latin America: an internationalist demand to end empire, to keep out of the Cold War blocs, to uphold sovereignty and non-interference, and to remake the world economy in favour of developing countries (Bandung 1955, the 1974 New International Economic Order). It was a coalition of states and intellectuals rather than a full social programme, so its sources are silent on most domestic questions.
